The executor needs to analyze each electrolyzer type:

1. Alkaline electrolyzer cells:
   - Traditional technology
   - Uses liquid electrolyte (KOH)
   - Moderate efficiency

   - Operates at lower temperatures

2. Anion exchange electrolyzer cells:
   - Newer technology
   - Uses solid polymer electrolyte
   - Higher efficiency than alkaline
   - Can use non-precious metal catalysts
   - Operates at lower temperatures

3. Proton exchange electrolyzer cells:
   - Uses solid polymer electrolyte
   - High efficiency
   - Requires precious metal catalysts (less sustainable)
   - Operates at lower temperatures
   - Requires high purity water

4. Solid oxide electrolyzer cells:
   - Operates at high temperatures (700-900°C)
   - Highest electrical efficiency
   - Can use waste heat (thermal integration)
   - Can operate in reverse as fuel cells
   - Doesn't require precious metal catalysts
   - Can use CO2 as input for co-electrolysis
